acceptanceCriteria: With a 45k-receipt journal, a writer committing every few seconds and 8 concurrent acquirers, every acquire completes within a documented bound (e.g. under 2 minutes).
CPU per waiting acquirer does not scale with the number of retries.
A test reproduces the starvation with a synthetic journal and a background writer and passes after the fix.
Spec records the bound and the admission/audit-reuse rule with requirement IDs.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1010 (author ls-russell-lewis, opened 2026-10-17), observed on 1.0.0-rc.3 (main 8cd20e9). With a ~45,000-receipt journal, a 4-member all-FREE pool, a running dispatch and up to 8 concurrent pool acquire processes, acquires lived 2-42 minutes at 30-98% CPU while other writers committed (queue status ~0.2s, head.json advancing). Profile: leaseCommand -> store.Lease -> leaseOnce -> leaseWrite -> prepareLease -> journal.Reader.AuditForWriteObserved -> audit -> walk. Cause (suspected): the pool verb family stays on the complete route (a5827b719, 92000b394); each attempt re-walks the whole journal and is retried if any other write lands during the walk, so a long audit rarely wins under a steady write rate. Starvation, not deadlock. Suggested fixes: fair admission after audit, audit-once-per-head with incremental suffix audit, coalesced acquires, or a retryable result reporting retries and audit duration. See the issue for details.
title: pool acquire starves 10-40 min on a large journal: complete-route audit redone on every retry (issue #1010)
